cards.title: Branch creation timing relative to the first edit
cards.definition: When a version-control branch is created during the recorded work: before the first write to a project file, after edits have begun, or not at all.
cards.evidenceTest: Find branch-creating commands (git checkout -b, git switch -c, git branch) with a linked result, and the first call that writes or edits a project file. Compare their order. Check whether any write, test or commit follows the branch.
cards.nearMiss: A branch command that fails. Switching to an existing branch. Scratch writes outside the repository before the branch.

values.name: before the first edit
values.test: The branch is created before any write or edit to a project file.

values.name: after edits began
values.test: At least one project file is written or edited before the branch is created.

values.name: no branch created
values.test: No branch-creating command with a linked result appears in the trace.

values.name: branch with no change
values.test: A branch is created and the trace ends with no write, edit, test or commit on it.

cards.title: Named base branch missing: fallback disclosed or not
cards.definition: The task asks for a branch from a named base that the repository lacks. The agent branches from another base, and its final message either says so or does not.
cards.trigger: The task names a base branch, and a branch listing or a failed lookup shows that branch does not exist in the repository.
cards.evidenceTest: Confirm the named base from the task text and its absence from a linked branch listing, rev-parse or checkout error. Find the branch-creating command and the base it used. Read the final message for the base actually used.
cards.nearMiss: The named base exists. The task names no base. A clone or tag fallback that creates no branch.
cards.significance: A success line from a fallback can hide a deviation from the instruction. Disclosure is a separate fact that must be checked.

values.name: fallback disclosed
values.test: A message names the base actually used or says the requested base did not exist.

values.name: fallback not disclosed
values.test: The final message repeats the requested base or is silent about the substitution.

cards.title: Branch and commit state confirmed by repository output before handoff
cards.definition: Completion of a branch-and-commit requirement is established only by linked VCS outputs: when the branch was created relative to the first edit, a commit hash after any identity recovery, a clean status, and any later amend that changes the shipped state.
cards.evidenceTest: Locate the branch-creation result and compare its position with the first edit or write. Find the commit attempt and any author-identity failure, the repo-local config fix, and a commit result with a hash. Then look for status or log on the expected branch. For the negative case, confirm there is no commit call after the last edit.
cards.nearMiss: Successful branch creation alone. Also an agent summary claiming the work was committed with no status or log output.
cards.significance: Separates the shipped commit from intermediate states. Shows when the branch requirement was met only at the end, and when work was never committed.

cards.title: Commit completion requires a new commit result
cards.definition: A commit counts as existing only when a linked result reports a new hash that touches the agent's files. Failed attempts, stray stat output from the existing HEAD, test success, or narrative 'done' do not count.
cards.evidenceTest: Check for a commit call whose result shows a new SHA and file list, ideally followed by git log or status. Check whether file-change counts in a failed commit's output belong to the existing HEAD, for example by the author shown on a follow-up log.
cards.nearMiss: A trace with a green test run and a diff review but no commit call. Stat lines printed in the output of a failed commit.
cards.significance: This prevents branch and commit requirements from being credited on the basis of tests or summaries.

cards.title: Pending changes inspected before commit
cards.definition: Before staging or committing, the agent runs git status or git diff and uses the output to see what will be committed.
cards.evidenceTest: Find the commit call. Confirm an earlier git status or git diff call, after the last edit, with a linked result.
cards.nearMiss: Status or diff run only after the commit. A status call with no linked result. A diff run before later edits.

cards.title: Staging scope before commit
cards.definition: How the agent selects what enters the commit: by naming paths, or by staging everything in the working tree. Build shims, regenerated files and unrelated modifications enter the commit or stay out depending on that choice.
cards.trigger: A staging command in the record: git add in any form, or git commit -a.
cards.evidenceTest: Read the arguments of each staging command before the commit. Record whether a git status or staged diff runs between staging and the commit, and compare the commit's file list with the intended change where one is recorded.
cards.nearMiss: A commit made by the harness with no staging call in the trace. Cleanup of scratch files with no staging or commit.

values.name: explicit paths
values.test: git add names the files or directories of the intended change.

values.name: everything
values.test: git add -A, git add . or git commit -a stages the whole working tree.

cards.title: Documentation updated with the behavior change
cards.definition: When a change alters what users see (a CLI, API, schema or output), the agent also edits the matching documentation, changelog or expected-output fixtures.
cards.evidenceTest: Find the implementation edit and a later edit to a documentation, changelog or fixture file that describes the same behavior.
cards.nearMiss: Documentation edits that the task names as the main deliverable. Comments inside the changed source file.

cards.title: Placement of new logic: dedicated module or inline
cards.definition: Runs on the same task place the same behavior either in a new module imported by consumers or inline in an existing service or models file. This changes file counts, edit stability, testability in isolation, and constraints on type ownership.
cards.evidenceTest: Find a write that creates a new module followed by import edits, compared with patches or splices that add the code to an existing file. Confirm file counts from commit stats or create-mode lines. Note any repeated region rewrites or duplicated-block recovery in the inline case, and any import-cycle fix in the module case.
cards.nearMiss: A summary listing utilities with no file-creation evidence. Also, in-file placement with a stated rationale that converges cleanly. Inline placement is not the failure pattern by itself.
cards.significance: Placement predicts where reviewers and tests attach. It also predicts how stable large edits will be.

values.name: dedicated module
values.test: The new behavior lives in a new file, and existing files gain only imports or thin calls into it.

values.name: inline
values.test: The new behavior is written into an existing file.

cards.title: Widening a shared base contract that downstream code consumes
cards.definition: A feature is added by placing a new type, prop or protected hook on a common base interface, base class or shared parser state. Separate edits then wire consumers to the new member, instead of each call site being patched locally.
cards.evidenceTest: Look for an edit request that adds a member to a base or shared module, and separate consumer edits that import or call it. Check each linked result for applied versus error status. Count only edits whose result reports success as executed.
cards.nearMiss: A base-contract edit whose linked result is an error, while only a consumer import succeeded. The design was proposed but its definition is not shown as applied.
cards.significance: This captures a cross-cutting choice that shapes later edits. It keeps the design apart from whether the edits actually landed.

cards.title: Speculative interface widening for hypothetical consumers
cards.definition: Without a spec requirement or an observed failure, the agent widens shared helpers, public types or routes, justified by unseen callers or tests.
cards.trigger: An agent message that justifies an edit by callers, tests or inputs it has not seen, in wording such as 'in case', 'defensive', 'hidden tests may' or 'for compatibility with'.
cards.evidenceTest: Find the triggering message and the edit that follows it. Confirm the edit widens what a shared helper, public type, export or route accepts beyond the task statement. Confirm no failing result and no specification text asks for it.
cards.nearMiss: Edits made after a recorded failure. New public surface the task asks for. Internal refactoring with no change to what is accepted or exported.
cards.significance: Flags scope creep and guesses about grading.

cards.title: Building on existing host extension interfaces versus new engine internals
cards.definition: A feature is built either by threading new hooks into engine internals, or by reusing an existing host facility such as a tracer stream or the linter's type information. The reuse may come only after an assumed helper is found not to exist.
cards.evidenceTest: Check for edits or new options at engine evaluation sites, compared with an implementation confined to consumer-layer files plus a diff stat that excludes the engine. Or check for an agent statement naming the missing helper and the existing facility, followed by edits and build-error fixes.
cards.nearMiss: Extensive reading of engine internals with no edits shipped there.
cards.significance: Where the feature hooks in decides the blast radius and how much debugging the engine semantics need.

values.name: existing host interface
values.test: The feature reuses an existing host facility or extension point.

values.name: new engine internals
values.test: The feature threads new hooks into the engine's internals.

cards.title: Parallel implementations of one behavior: all edited, some, or one
cards.definition: The same behavior is implemented once per dialect, backend or language. The agent's change reaches all of the copies, some of them with a stated limit, or only one.
cards.trigger: The changed behavior has two or more separate implementations in the repository, per dialect, backend, language or runtime-and-type pair, shown by sibling files or directories the agent lists or reads.
cards.evidenceTest: List the variant implementations from the record. For each, check for an edit with variant-specific content and a linked success result. Record any stated limit and any test that compares variants.
cards.nearMiss: Several call sites in one file changed by one replace-all. A repository with a single implementation. Identical code pasted into every variant where each needs its own mechanism.
cards.significance: This tells a reviewer which call sites must be checked for drift. Parity is only as strong as the tested range.

values.name: all variants edited
values.test: Each variant's file has an edit and a linked success result.

values.name: some edited, limit stated
values.test: Some variants are edited and a message or code path states that the rest are unsupported.

values.name: one variant only
values.test: One variant is edited and the others are neither edited nor mentioned.

cards.title: Artifact coupled to one sampled snapshot versus derived from the source domain
cards.definition: A shipped artifact is either derived from a specific sample, such as explored positions or one build's hash and copied file, or generated from the full domain or the live source directory. That choice decides whether the artifact can survive new inputs or rebuilds.
cards.trigger: The deliverable includes a data artifact the agent generates or writes by hand: a lookup table, a rule set, an index, a mapping, or a configuration that pins a hash or file name.
cards.evidenceTest: Find how the artifact was produced. On the sample side, look for rules built from the inputs the agent happened to inspect, or a value copied from one build's output. On the source side, look for a generator that enumerates the whole domain or reads the live source directory. Record later coverage gaps separately.
cards.nearMiss: Ordinary source edits. A scratch sample used only for testing. A smaller output or a passing install taken alone.
cards.significance: A reported pass means different things depending on whether the artifact can generalize beyond the sampled snapshot.

values.name: derived from a sample
values.test: The artifact is built from one sampled snapshot, such as explored positions or one build's hash.

values.name: derived from the source domain
values.test: The artifact is generated from the full domain or the live source directory.

cards.title: Bulk local materialization versus per-item remote fan-out
cards.definition: One run downloads the whole reference collection once and joins it locally. Another issues one network request per candidate and aggregates responses that may be partial.
cards.trigger: The task needs data about many items from a remote source, and the record shows at least one network call that fetches it.
cards.evidenceTest: Find how the data arrives. One call that produces a whole-collection artifact followed by local reads and joins is bulk materialization. Calls that iterate identifiers over the network, with results keyed per identifier and some missing, are fan-out.
cards.nearMiss: A single download of one file. Work on data already present locally. Many requests batched inside one code cell, which is still fan-out.
cards.significance: Missing results in fan-out may be transport gaps, not absent records.

values.name: bulk local materialization
values.test: The whole reference collection is downloaded once and joined locally.

values.name: per-item remote fan-out
values.test: One network request is issued per candidate and the responses are aggregated.
